issues.on_page: Capital Outlay: Equipment 20,350.94 (Fire Department Fund column only)
issues.issue: capital outlay printed only in the Fire Department Fund column, which names the function (public safety); the capital outlay rule allows 'Capital Outlay: Public Safety'. Same for disbursements[16] (Buildings 6,700.00) and detail[32]/detail[33] (p14, Fire Department Fund column)

issues.on_page: Sales Tax 6,618.66 (Operating Receipts, Total Proprietary Funds)
issues.issue: sales tax collected on utility bills and remitted to the state ('Sales Tax Remittance' 6,671.32); the Statement of Activities (p2) counts it in Charges for Services (92,532.24 / 38,842.71). Recording it as the village's sales tax revenue may overstate local sales tax; same for detail[48] (Water 4,631.71) and detail[59] (Sewer 1,986.95). Remittance detail_category 'tax refunds/treasurer fees' (detail[55], detail[64]) is also a loose fit

utility cost-type rule says lines that are a function (e.g. 'Operating expenses') stay 'utilities'; the 'Operating' category rule applies to lines with no function. Judgment call; same for detail[50] and detail[61]

cross-year: FY2023 ending governmental balance 509,635.01 (General 17,704.86, Fire Department 360,917.60, Ball Park 61,722.53, Street 66,955.85, Bank Building 2,334.17) does not equal the FY2024 waiver beginning (General 16,934.78, Fire Department 109,908.18; Street, Ball Park and Bank Building tie). No restatement is printed in the FY2023 report; the difference sits in the FY2024 filing's Fire Department and General columns. Business-type ending 2,388.15 = FY2024 beginning 2,388.15 (ties)
